q: What is the CBAM default value for cement and clinker from India?
title: CBAM default value: Indian cement, clinker
short: Indian grey clinker carries 1.440 t CO2e per tonne and grey Portland cement 1.480, both including indirect emissions from electricity. White clinker is 1.410, white Portland cement 1.470 and aluminous cement 2.290. Cement counts indirect emissions, unlike steel and aluminium.
audience: Indian cement and clinker exporters and their EU importers

sections.h: India default values, t CO2e per tonne (direct + indirect = total)
ul: Calcined clay and other hydraulic cements: no India value listed

p: The listed values are increased by a mark-up: 10% for 2026, 20% for 2027 and 30% from 2028. Goods imported in 2026 always take the 2026 mark-up.
Portland pozzolana and slag cements contain less clinker, so their actual embedded emissions are usually well below 1.480. The importer must report clinker content, so keep it on record per batch.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so an actual figure you send an EU buyer can be traced back to the documents behind it. It does not file CBAM declarations.
